message.content: {"0": {"original": "signed a deal with Warner Brothers to host WBTV-branded content", "rephrased": "The startup Joost is securing content agreements with major studios, such as Warner Brothers, to host branded programming. This strategic move establishes Joost as a key aggregator for on-demand, freely distributed online television, aiming to balance consumer flexibility with industry control despite challenges regarding content quality and bandwidth efficiency.", "summary": "Joost secures studio deals to become a major provider of free, on-demand online TV."}, "1": {"original": "made deals with other providers like Time Warner and Sony Pictures Television", "rephrased": "By expanding content partnerships with major providers like Time Warner and Sony Pictures Television, the startup Joost is solidifying its position as a primary aggregator for on-demand, freely distributed online television. This broadened portfolio allows the service to offer a wide variety of channels, effectively balancing the consumer desire for choice with the entertainment industry's need to retain control over their intellectual property.", "summary": "Joost expands studio partnerships to offer a wide range of free, on-demand TV channels."}, "2": {"original": "became the aggregator and provider for on-demand, freely distributed online TV", "rephrased": "The startup Joost has emerged as the leading aggregator and provider for on-demand, freely distributed online television broadcasts by leveraging peer-to-peer networking technology. This approach allows the service to offer free programming that balances consumer flexibility with industry control, aiming to solve the bandwidth inefficiencies inherent in traditional distribution models while navigating the complexities of securing high-quality content rights.", "summary": "Joost uses peer-to-peer tech to become the leading provider of free, on-demand online TV."}, "3": {"original": "Joost offers 150 channels with full-screen quality, though availability varies", "rephrased": "The startup Joost currently provides approximately 150 channels featuring full-screen, eye-quality television, although the availability of specific channels varies by country or region due to copyright restrictions. This service allows viewers to navigate menus and interact with programming through integrated widgets, representing a significant step forward in delivering a flexible, high-quality online TV experience that competes with established cable and satellite models.", "summary": "Joost offers 150 high-quality channels with interactive features, subject to regional copyright limits."}}
